sentences.text: Researchers administered a traditional Chinese medicine extract to healthy adult mice and created a rat model of premenstrual dysphoric disorder using repeated stress, then measured anxiety and depression-like behaviors with standard tests.
The extract reduced signs of depression and anxiety in the mice and significantly improved behaviors associated with anxiety and despair in the stressed rats.

Using qRT-PCR, a molecular biology technique, the study found that the extract restored reduced levels of two specific GABA receptor subunit genes in the hippocampus while leaving the other four tested subunits unchanged.
Computer simulations identified paeoniflorin as the compound among those tested that showed specific binding activity at a particular site on the GABA receptors.
Electrical recordings from neurons confirmed that paeoniflorin changed the flow of chloride ions triggered by GABA in a concentration-dependent manner.
